public_rationale: The inspected release reports mathematical results and does not establish performance outside mathematics. That supports a narrower concern about missing transfer evidence. It does not establish Marcus's stronger claim that there was no informative basis at all, or that the missing procedural details caused that state. Evaluations of other models and disclosures made later cannot resolve the claim as written.
limitations: Absence of a located benchmark is not proof that no applicable evidence existed.
Mathematical discoveries with possible scientific applications are not direct measurements of broader model capability.

from_speaker: how generalizable the result is outside math
our_interpretation: Read as a claim that the missing disclosures leave no substantive public basis for assessing transfer beyond mathematics.
This concerns evidence available when Marcus wrote, not a prediction that the model will fail outside mathematics.
Outside mathematics excludes mathematical proofs merely motivated by physics or theoretical computer science; empirical performance on materially different tasks would count.
The causal component requires more than finding no non-mathematical benchmark in the announcement: the missing information must account for the claimed inability to assess transfer.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous evidence establishes that the missing disclosures prevent a substantive assessment of transfer, with no applicable public evidence about the same system outside mathematics.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Contemporaneous, system-matched evidence provides a substantive basis for assessing performance outside mathematics despite the missing disclosures, or otherwise defeats the asserted causal explanation.
